title: The Pedigree as a Model Test

scenes.tts: Can one family observation eliminate an inheritance model? Watch this pedigree become a test instead of a pattern to memorize. The answer depends on what each model says should be possible. This is why a pedigree works like a model test.
scenes.caption: Can one family observation eliminate an inheritance model? Watch this pedigree become a test instead of a pattern to memorize. The answer depends on what each model says should be possible. This is why a pedigree works like a model test.
scenes.visual: COLOUR MAP FOR BOTH FILMS: inheritance routes GOLD; affected phenotypes RED; compatible model marks TEAL; contradictions VIOLET; unaffected symbols WHITE. Fill the frame with one three-generation pedigree on a dark background. Family symbols draw themselves outward from the founding pair while a large question mark follows the connecting lines.
scenes.narration: Can one family observation eliminate an inheritance model? Watch this pedigree become a test instead of a pattern to memorize. The answer depends on what each model says should be possible. This is why a pedigree works like a model test.

scenes.visual: The pedigree keeps breathing with subtle line motion. Title 'The Pedigree as a Model Test' appears briefly above it, then transforms into a small label at top left.

scenes.tts: A pedigree records people, relationships, and a named phenotype. Shapes identify family members, connecting lines show relationships, and fill marks affected people. Always read its key. The same symbol can mean something different when the chart defines it differently.
scenes.caption: A pedigree records people, relationships, and a named phenotype. Shapes identify family members, connecting lines show relationships, and fill marks affected people. Always read its key. The same symbol can mean something different when the chart defines it differently.
scenes.visual: Keep the same pedigree. Enlarge one WHITE square, one WHITE circle, and one RED filled symbol in place as each is named. Relationship lines brighten from partners to their children. A compact key grows beside the chart, then docks at lower left.
scenes.narration: A pedigree records people, relationships, and a named phenotype. Shapes identify family members, connecting lines show relationships, and fill marks affected people. Always read its key. The same symbol can mean something different when the chart defines it differently.

scenes.tts: Now place a model over the chart. Each inheritance model predicts where an allele can travel and which relatives can receive it. The chart becomes evidence because every line now makes a claim.
scenes.caption: Now place a model over the chart. Each inheritance model predicts where an allele can travel and which relatives can receive it. The chart becomes evidence because every line now makes a claim.
scenes.visual: A transparent model card slides behind the pedigree. GOLD paths begin at one founder and animate along possible parent-child routes. A TEAL check follows each route that remains compatible with the visible phenotypes.
scenes.narration: Now place a model over the chart. Each inheritance model predicts where an allele can travel and which relatives can receive it. The chart becomes evidence because every line now makes a claim.

scenes.tts: An autosomal route can move through either parent and either sex. A dominant model lets an affected heterozygous parent pass the allele to children of either sex. An affected child of two unaffected parents contradicts that simple dominant model.
scenes.caption: An autosomal route can move through either parent and either sex. A dominant model lets an affected heterozygous parent pass the allele to children of either sex. An affected child of two unaffected parents contradicts that simple dominant model.
scenes.visual: The GOLD route branches through a mother and father to children represented by different shapes. Label the model card 'autosomal dominant — schematic'. The route pulses downward from a RED affected parent while unaffected branches stay WHITE.
scenes.narration: An autosomal route can move through either parent and either sex. A dominant model lets an affected heterozygous parent pass the allele to children of either sex. An affected child of two unaffected parents contradicts that simple dominant model.

scenes.tts: A recessive allele can hide in unaffected carriers. It may appear among siblings when each parent contributes a recessive allele. Here, unaffected parents can carry the allele without showing the trait.
scenes.caption: A recessive allele can hide in unaffected carriers. It may appear among siblings when each parent contributes a recessive allele. Here, unaffected parents can carry the allele without showing the trait.
scenes.visual: Transform the model label to 'autosomal recessive — schematic'. Put a small GOLD half-fill marker beside each unaffected parent, defined on screen as 'carrier'. Their routes converge on a RED affected child while another child remains WHITE.
scenes.narration: A recessive allele can hide in unaffected carriers. It may appear among siblings when each parent contributes a recessive allele. Here, unaffected parents can carry the allele without showing the trait.

scenes.tts: Sex-linked models restrict the route. A father gives his ex chromosome to daughters and his why chromosome to sons. That route makes sex and parental origin informative, not merely decorative.
scenes.caption: Sex-linked models restrict the route. A father gives his X chromosome to daughters and his Y chromosome to sons. That route makes sex and parental origin informative, not merely decorative.
scenes.visual: Zoom to one father with a daughter and son. Two labelled chromosome bars emerge: GOLD 'X' travels to the daughter; GREY 'Y' travels to the son. The rest of the pedigree stays dim but visible.
scenes.narration: Sex-linked models restrict the route. A father gives his X chromosome to daughters and his Y chromosome to sons. That route makes sex and parental origin informative, not merely decorative.

scenes.tts: An affected father also has an affected son. Could an ex-linked allele have travelled directly from that father to that son? Follow the chromosome route before you answer.
scenes.caption: An affected father also has an affected son. Could an X-linked allele have travelled directly from that father to that son? Follow the chromosome route before you answer.
scenes.visual: Keep the father and son large. A dotted GOLD question path tries to connect them. Show the question 'Direct X-linked transmission?' above the pair while the maternal X route waits offscreen.
scenes.narration: An affected father also has an affected son. Could an X-linked allele have travelled directly from that father to that son? Follow the chromosome route before you answer.

scenes.visual: Deliberate prediction pause. The dotted question path shimmers slowly; chromosome bars drift gently. No answer appears.

scenes.tts: No. The son's ex chromosome came from his mother. Demonstrated father-to-son transmission therefore contradicts both ex-linked models under these assumptions. An affected pair alone shows it only if the mother carries no copy.
scenes.caption: No. The son's X chromosome came from his mother. Demonstrated father-to-son transmission therefore contradicts both X-linked models under these assumptions. An affected pair alone shows it only if the mother carries no copy.
scenes.visual: The dotted father-son path dissolves. A GOLD X route enters from the mother and reaches the son. A VIOLET contradiction bar crosses the X-linked model card, labelled 'father-to-son transmission'. Keep both model labels neutral.
scenes.narration: No. The son's X chromosome came from his mother. Demonstrated father-to-son transmission therefore contradicts both X-linked models under these assumptions. An affected pair alone shows it only if the mother carries no copy.

scenes.tts: Mitochondrial inheritance draws a different route. Mothers can transmit mitochondrial D N A to children, while fathers normally transmit none. This maternal route differs from mitochondrial diseases caused by nuclear genes.
scenes.caption: Mitochondrial inheritance draws a different route. Mothers can transmit mitochondrial DNA to children, while fathers normally transmit none. This maternal route differs from mitochondrial diseases caused by nuclear genes.
scenes.visual: Restore the full pedigree. GOLD mitochondrial dots flow from an affected mother into every child symbol. At an affected father, the dots circulate inside his symbol but no child route appears. Label this model 'mitochondrial — simple model'.
scenes.narration: Mitochondrial inheritance draws a different route. Mothers can transmit mitochondrial DNA to children, while fathers normally transmit none. This maternal route differs from mitochondrial diseases caused by nuclear genes.

scenes.tts: Fitting predictions support a model; one contradiction can rule it out. Compatibility adds support, but an observation the model forbids carries sharper information. The model earns confidence by surviving such tests. That is the guiding rule for this simple-model test.
scenes.caption: Fitting predictions support a model; one contradiction can rule it out. Compatibility adds support, but an observation the model forbids carries sharper information. The model earns confidence by surviving such tests. That is the guiding rule for this simple-model test.
scenes.visual: The pedigree shifts left. Model cards stack at right. For each card, GOLD routes animate over the same family; TEAL marks compatible observations and VIOLET marks one contradiction. A magnifying glass travels from prediction to observation.
scenes.narration: Fitting predictions support a model; one contradiction can rule it out. Compatibility adds support, but an observation the model forbids carries sharper information. The model earns confidence by surviving such tests. That is the guiding rule for this simple-model test.

scenes.tts: That test has a scope. It assumes full penetrance, no new mutation, correct relationships, and the simple model being tested. Change an assumption, and a seeming contradiction may need another explanation.
scenes.caption: That test has a scope. It assumes full penetrance, no new mutation, correct relationships, and the simple model being tested. Change an assumption, and a seeming contradiction may need another explanation.
scenes.visual: Four scope labels appear around the model-card frame, never over the pedigree. Each label locks one corner of the frame. The routes remain animated, but VIOLET contradiction marks soften when the frame is opened.
scenes.narration: That test has a scope. It assumes full penetrance, no new mutation, correct relationships, and the simple model being tested. Change an assumption, and a seeming contradiction may need another explanation.

scenes.tts: A fitting chart supports a model without proving it. Other models or hidden biology may predict the same small family. Small families often lack the relative who would distinguish those models.
scenes.caption: A fitting chart supports a model without proving it. Other models or hidden biology may predict the same small family. Small families often lack the relative who would distinguish those models.
scenes.visual: Two model cards project different GOLD routes that both fit the visible pedigree. Both receive modest TEAL marks. The word 'supports' appears between them; no winner or certainty icon appears.
scenes.narration: A fitting chart supports a model without proving it. Other models or hidden biology may predict the same small family. Small families often lack the relative who would distinguish those models.

scenes.visual: End card shows one line only: 'Fitting predictions support a model; one contradiction can rule it out.' The pedigree lines continue a very slow GOLD trace behind the text.
